name: aiogram-pdk-ots
instr:
The repository at `/workdir` is aiogram, an asynchronous Python framework for building Telegram bots. Its
update-routing layer decides which handler sees each incoming update: a Dispatcher and a tree of Routers hold
event observers, handlers are registered on them with filters (plain functions, coroutines, `Filter`
subclasses, magic filters and their logical combinations), middlewares wrap the handling, and the context
data that filters and middlewares produce is injected into handlers as keyword arguments.

Fix all implementation drift from the documentation in this part of the repository.
Everything in scope is aiogram's update-routing layer: the dispatcher package (aiogram/dispatcher/: the Dispatcher, routers, event observers and handler objects, middlewares and flags), the filters package (aiogram/filters/), the class-based handlers (aiogram/handlers/), aiogram's magic-filter extension (aiogram/utils/magic_filter.py) and its exceptions module (aiogram/exceptions.py), together with the documentation pages under docs/dispatcher/ except the finite-state-machine pages and webhook.rst, the example scripts those pages include (examples/echo_bot.py, examples/own_filter.py and examples/context_addition_from_filter.py), and the module, class and function docstrings of the in-scope modules.

Where the code and the documentation disagree about runtime behavior, the documentation is the
authority: change the implementation so that it does what the documentation says, and do not edit
